details: Escalating conflict between the United States and Iran in the Middle East, including missile barrages, has caused Brent crude to leap 7.3% to settle at $88.09 per barrel. This led to a sell-off on Wall Street, with the S&P 500 falling 1.5%. Investors are also closely watching the Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates unchanged, amidst concerns about inflation and slower global economic growth.
title: Oil Prices Jump, Stocks Fall Amid Escalating Middle East Tensions

details: Rostec, Russia's state defense corporation, has quietly launched a new ruble token named RubX. This move comes despite further EU sanctions targeting Russian crypto markets. Cryptocurrencies are increasingly being used by Russian importers to bypass Western sanctions and facilitate international payments, with RubX offering swaps to the widely used dollar stablecoin Tether via Telegram.
title: Russia's Defense Sector Launches New Cryptocurrency Amid EU Sanctions

details: Iran and Hezbollah are increasingly leveraging cryptocurrencies to bypass international sanctions, facilitate fund transfers for sanctioned oil sales, and procure weapons. A Reuters investigation found that an illicit Iranian gambling network channeled at least $4 billion through Shelbit, an unlicensed Dubai-based cryptocurrency exchange, which also processed funds for sanctioned Iranian institutions.
title: Iran & Hezbollah Use Crypto for Illicit Operations, Sanctions Evasion

details: The Madras High Court in India has ruled that cryptocurrency tokens held on an exchange constitute "property" and are therefore subject to trust obligations. This decision provides significant legal clarity on the proprietary nature of digital assets, custodial relationships, and interim protection of crypto holdings in India, particularly important as the country currently lacks a comprehensive regulatory framework for cryptocurrency.
title: Indian Court Recognizes Cryptocurrency as 'Property'

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) published the results of its 2026 thematic reverse stress test, which assessed how 110 euro area banks would be affected by severe geopolitical scenarios, aiming for at least a 300-basis point depletion in their Common Equity Tier 1 capital. Geopolitical risk remains a key supervisory priority for the ECB, highlighting ongoing global economic uncertainty.
title: ECB Conducts Geopolitical Risk Stress Test on Euro Area Banks
